A_target.statement:
In the [[Definition:Tropical Semiring|tropical semiring]] $\struct {\R \cup \set \infty, \min, +}$, a [[Definition:Tropical Polynomial|tropical polynomial]]:
:$\map p x = \displaystyle \min_i \paren {c_i + i x}$
is a piecewise linear [[Definition:Concave Real Function|concave]] function, and its tropical zero set is the locus where the minimum is attained at least twice.

B_source.statement:
Let $K$ be a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]].
A [[Definition:Polynomial over Ring|polynomial]] $\displaystyle \sum_i c_i x^i$ over $K$ has [[Definition:Root of Polynomial|zero set]] $\set {x: \map p x = 0}$.

derived.a polynomial as a formal combination of: a minimum of finitely many affine functions
derived.the zero set of a polynomial: the locus where the minimum is attained at least twice

object_map.reformulation: Reinterpret the two field operations as minimum and addition, keeping the polynomial syntax and rebuilding the notion of a root.

validity_conditions: The tropical semiring satisfies associativity, commutativity, and distributivity, so polynomial syntax transfers verbatim.
Additive inverses do not exist, so any argument using subtraction fails; this is the main structural difference and it rules out most of linear algebra in the usual form.
The notion of a root must be redefined, since the additive unit is rarely attained; the standard replacement is the locus where the minimum is achieved by at least two terms.
proof_plan:
Replace addition by $\min$ and multiplication by $+$.
$\struct {\R \cup \set \infty, \min, +}$ satisfies the [[Definition:Semiring (Abstract Algebra)|semiring axioms]], with identities $\infty$ and $0$.

Reinterpreting $\displaystyle \sum_i c_i x^i$ gives:
:$\displaystyle \map p x = \min_i \paren {c_i + i x}$
a minimum of affine functions, hence piecewise linear and concave.

Arguments using only the semiring axioms survive, such as expansion of products.
Arguments using subtraction do not, as $\min$ has no inverses; for example $\min \set {x, x} = x$ cannot be cancelled.

Redefine the zero set as the non-differentiability locus of $p$, where the minimum is attained by at least two terms.
{{qed}}
